metadata.agent_last_message:
I've built the simulator in `output/` (`main.js`, `parser.js`, `interp.js`, `trace.js`), using only the Node standard library. It handles all the command-line options you listed. I ran the three examples from your requirements and got the expected trace entries and exit codes. I also ran the three sample programs from Appendix C of the spec, plus my own tests covering cutter compensation, all the canned cycles, probing, G28, G92/G10, inch/mm switching, inverse-time feed, `%` files, block delete, parameter-file round trips and error exits. They all ran, but there's no official expected output to compare against, so beyond the examples, correctness is checked only by inspection and hand calculation.

**What it covers:**
- **Reading programs:** the full line syntax, including expressions, all the math functions, parameter references and settings, comments, line numbers, block delete and `%` start/end lines.
- **Execution:** each line runs in the order given in Table 8, with the modal groups and the error checks the spec documents. Errors exit with code 1 and still write both the result file and the trace. Code 2 is reserved for bugs in the simulator itself.
- **Machine model:** positions are tracked as absolute machine coordinates of the tool tip (including tool length offset) and reported in the current inch/mm units.
- **Cutter compensation:** follows Appendix B (entry moves, corner arcs, concave-corner and gouging errors), with R and I/J read the way `Clarifications.md` defines them.
- **Canned cycles:** G81–G89 are expanded into individual moves. G84, G86 and G87 change the spindle direction mid-cycle and restore it at the end. G88 retracts automatically as the clarification says. G87 treats missing I/J/K as 0.
- **Trace:** each entry records only what changed since the previous one, with the time, distance and position-tolerance sampling modes. It follows your rules on where changes and labels attach, carry-over entries at the end of a line, and errors part-way th

editorial.last_message: Claims broad support after examples and hand calculations, not reference testing. Five failures remain in G-code tolerance, rotary parameters, probe validation and rotary-only millimetre trace timing.
